title: Form Lead Tracking: Which Campaign Sent the Lead
h1: Form lead tracking: how to see which campaign sent each lead
description: Form lead tracking shows which campaign, ad or affiliate sent each web enquiry. Learn the steps to credit every lead to its real source.
faq: How do I track which campaign a form lead came from?
Give each campaign its own tracking link, record the traffic source when the visitor lands, and store it with the form submission so every lead carries its campaign.
Why do my form leads show as direct traffic?
Visitors often return later by typing your address, so the last visit looks direct. Capturing the source on the first visit and keeping it fixes this.
Should I track phone calls as well as form leads?
Yes. Many prospects phone instead of filling in a form, so tracking only forms makes call-driven campaigns look weaker than they are.
body:
Form lead tracking means recording, for every website form submission, which campaign, ad or affiliate sent the visitor, so you can credit the lead to its real source. The short version: capture the traffic source when the visitor lands, keep it until they submit the form, and store it next to the lead. Without that, a form lead is just a name and an email, and you cannot tell which marketing budget produced it.

Why form leads lose their source

A visitor clicks an ad on Monday, browses, leaves, and comes back on Thursday by typing your address. When they finally fill in the form, most systems record the visit that happened last, which looks like "direct". The ad that did the real work gets no credit, and the budget conversation that follows is based on guesses.

The same problem appears in every country. A clinic in Sydney, a property agent in Dubai, a training company in Bengaluru and a software firm in Berlin all pay for clicks and then need to know which ones turned into enquiries. The tools and customs differ by market, but the gap is the same.

What to capture with every form

  • Traffic source and medium: where the visitor came from, such as a paid ad, an email, a partner or an affiliate.
  • Campaign name: the specific campaign or affiliate link that was clicked.
  • Time of the click and time of the submission: so you can see how long leads take to convert.
  • The form or page: a quote form and a newsletter form are not the same kind of lead.

Step by step: how to track which campaign sent a form lead

  1. Give every campaign its own tracking link. Use a consistent naming pattern so "spring-search-ads" is never also written "Spring_Search". Consistency matters more than detail.
  2. Record the source on the first visit. Save it with the visitor session rather than relying on the last page they viewed.
  3. Attach the source to the form submission. The lead record should carry the campaign, not just the contact details.
  4. Compare against other lead types. Many businesses get leads by phone as well as forms. Looking at calls, clicks and form leads together shows which campaigns really work. See our guide to call tracking software for the phone side.
  5. Review weekly. Look at leads per campaign, then at how many became customers.

Do not forget the leads that start with a call

Form tracking alone undercounts. In many industries, such as home services, legal and insurance, a large share of prospects prefer to phone. If you only measure forms, the campaigns that drive calls look weak. Tracking numbers per campaign solve that by tracing each call to its source; see how call tracking works. For examples of how call-driven industries handle this, read about home services and legal campaigns.

Common mistakes

  • Mixed naming: three spellings of one campaign split its results into three rows.
  • Counting only the last click: repeat visitors hide the campaign that first brought them.
  • Ignoring lead quality: a campaign with many form fills but no customers is not a winner. Pass the outcome back to the source once you know it.
  • Forgetting privacy rules: consent for cookies, tracking and form data differs by country. Check your obligations with your own legal counsel before you launch.

What to do next

Pick your three biggest campaigns, give each its own tracking link, and check next week whether every form lead shows a source. If many still say "direct", your capture step is missing something. Once forms are tracked, add phone calls so the picture is complete.
